page: Amazon Web Services c7a.medium is an entry-tier compute-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro System and driven by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. Based on the x86_64 architecture, the server provides 1 dedicated vCPU mapped to a single physical core without multi-threading overhead, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. Memory capacity is configured at 2.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, establishing a standard 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio. The instance does not feature local storage volumes or GPU hardware, requiring remote network storage for persistent file systems. Processor capabilities include cryptographic extensions and vector instruction sets such as AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support.

Benchmark results reflect the instance's isolated single-core configuration. The dedicated 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC core demonstrates strong single-threaded performance in stress-ng evaluations, reaching 3031.18 points to place in the top quartile of tested hardware. Single-core Geekbench scores reach 1943.0, with single-threaded data throughput evaluating at 29.24 GB/sec for gzip compression and 13.53 GB/sec for bzip3 decompression. Conversely, multi-core aggregate metrics and memory-intensive evaluations rank in the lower percentiles due to the single-thread execution limit and 2.0 GB RAM capacity. Potentially uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 34.27 GB/sec, while write operations reach 28.35 GB/sec.

The hardware configuration provides an economical footprint for single-threaded processing that requires predictable CPU access without allocating larger multi-core resources. With its modern instruction extensions and high memory frequency, c7a.medium is appropriate for lightweight web microservices, small API gateways, single-threaded background jobs, CI/CD utility steps, and simple data transformation scripts.
description: Amazon Web Services c7a.medium is an entry-level compute-optimized instance driven by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 1 dedicated physical core running at 3.7 GHz alongside 2.0 GB of DDR5 system memory clocked at 5 GHz, adhering to a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server includes no integrated local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage for persistence. In benchmark tests, the single dedicated core demonstrates strong single-threaded computational throughput in stress-ng and standard compression workloads, while multi-threaded capacity and total throughput remain limited by the single-core profile. The instance represents an efficient entry-tier option for CPU-bound utility tasks, lightweight microservices, continuous integration build jobs, and basic web routing.
